lessons.trigger: When optimizing ERA5 regular-grid Zarr for tensor_loading.v1 full-field C,H,W reads.
lessons.recommendation: Use explicit sample-access-aligned chunks: one time sample and one selector plane per chunk, with the full selected latitude and longitude extents, while preserving all dimensions and channels.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines with full-field tensor consumer workloads.
lessons.evidence: The feasible parent passed all constraints but measured 30.9009 consumer_samples_per_second with 197 chunk objects for 28 samples and 3 channels; the workload read shuffled full C,H,W tensors.
lessons.caveat: This trajectory contains no measured alternate layout, so the chunking recommendation is a plausible engineering hypothesis rather than proven causation.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing footprint for ERA5 regular-grid Zarr where diagnostics separate chunk and metadata bytes.
lessons.recommendation: Target explicit deterministic lossless compression of data chunks before metadata tweaks, because the measured footprint is almost entirely chunk payload. Keep semantic content and artifact declarations unchanged.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines with decoded float32 ERA5 pressure-level arrays and consolidated metadata.
lessons.evidence: The feasible parent passed all hard constraints with output_bytes 175,189,531; diagnostics reported chunk_bytes 175,164,494 and metadata_bytes 25,037.
lessons.caveat: This identifies where bytes are concentrated in one trajectory; it does not prove that any specific compressor or level will reduce bytes on every fixture.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing footprint for ERA5 pressure-level regular-grid Zarr after the sample-aligned full-spatial chunk layout is already feasible.
lessons.recommendation: Prefer high-strength lossless Blosc-Zstd with bitshuffle for float32 data chunks before considering throughput-biased codecs; preserve the validated chunk topology and artifact declarations.
lessons.scope: ERA5 pressure-level Zarr v3 pipelines for tensor_loading.v1 full-field C,H,W reads with decoded float32 arrays.
lessons.evidence: Measured feasible trajectories: Blosc-Zstd clevel 7 bitshuffle output_bytes 108,202,642; Blosc-Zstd clevel 3 about 111,163,324; LZ4 bitshuffle about 128,426,256; LZ4/shuffle about 168.8 MB; uncompressed about 348.9 MB. All cited feasible runs passed hard constraints.
lessons.caveat: These are single noisy trajectory measurements on one fixture and do not prove the codec caused every byte difference or that clevel 7/9 is always optimal.

lessons.trigger: When optimizing footprint for ERA5 pressure-level Zarr after Blosc-Zstd bitshuffle compression is already feasible.
lessons.recommendation: Use or keep lossless Blosc-Zstd bitshuffle at clevel 9 for decoded float32 data chunks before trying weaker throughput-biased encodings; validate the codec by reopening and inspecting Zarr v3 metadata.
lessons.scope: ERA5 pressure-level regular-grid Zarr v3 pipelines with sample/selector/full-spatial chunks and exact semantic-equivalence requirements.
lessons.evidence: A feasible clevel 9 bitshuffle run passed all hard constraints with output_bytes 104,831,028. Earlier feasible measured runs included clevel 7 bitshuffle at 108,202,642, clevel 3 around 111,163,324, LZ4 bitshuffle around 128,426,256, and uncompressed around 348.9 MB.
lessons.caveat: These are noisy single-trajectory measurements on one fixture; they support a bounded preference but do not prove clevel 9 will always minimize bytes.

lessons.trigger: When multiple requested ERA5 pressure-level channels share the same source variable.
lessons.recommendation: Consider publishing one native array per source variable with a real selected pressure-level dimension and selector chunk size 1, then map each field-selector channel through artifact selectors instead of duplicating one array per channel.
lessons.scope: Regular-grid Zarr artifact layouts whose consumer/interface supports channel selectors and selector_coordinate_paths.
lessons.evidence: A prior feasible grouped-array trajectory passed all hard constraints for full-field tensor loading with uncompressed chunks and source-variable grouping; it preserved requested channels and measured output_bytes in the same range as uncompressed separate-array trajectories.
lessons.caveat: The observed byte difference in uncompressed runs was small and mixed, so grouping is mainly a compatibility-proven metadata-reduction tactic, not proven to improve every footprint run.
